history.q: Which Portuguese navigator reached the coast of Brazil in 1500?
history.fact: Cabral's fleet was on its way to India when it landed near present-day Porto Seguro, in Bahia, and claimed the land for Portugal.

history.q: Which city was Brazil's capital immediately before Brasília?
history.fact: Rio served as capital from 1763 until 1960 and is still nicknamed the "Cidade Maravilhosa" (Marvelous City).

history.q: Brazil takes its name from a tree prized by early traders for what?
history.fact: Brazilwood (pau-brasil) gets its name from "brasa," Portuguese for ember, after the glowing red color of its heartwood.

history.q: In what year did Brazil declare independence from Portugal?
history.fact: Prince Pedro declared independence beside the Ipiranga stream near São Paulo on 7 September 1822, reportedly crying "Independence or death!"

history.q: Which 1494 treaty divided newly found lands between Spain and Portugal, placing eastern South America in Portugal's sphere?
history.fact: The treaty drew a north-south line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands; lands east of it went to Portugal.

history.q: Who became Brazil's first emperor after independence?
history.fact: Pedro I later abdicated and returned to Europe; he also briefly reigned in Portugal as King Pedro IV.

history.q: In which year did Brazil become a republic, ending its monarchy?
history.fact: Emperor Pedro II was deposed in a military coup on 15 November 1889 and spent his final years in exile in Europe.

history.q: In what year was Brasília inaugurated as Brazil's capital?
history.fact: Built from scratch on the central plateau, Brasília is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the few 20th-century cities with that status.

history.q: What was the name of the 1888 law that abolished slavery in Brazil?
history.fact: Signed by Princess Isabel on 13 May 1888, it made Brazil the last country in the Americas to abolish slavery.

history.q: From 1808 to 1821, which European royal court was based in Rio de Janeiro?
history.fact: Fleeing Napoleon's invasion of Portugal, the royal family sailed to Brazil, making Rio the seat of the Portuguese Empire.

technology.q: Which Brazilian aviation pioneer flew the 14-bis airplane in Paris in 1906?
technology.fact: Santos-Dumont helped popularize the wristwatch: his friend Louis Cartier designed one so he could check the time without letting go of the controls.

technology.q: Which Brazilian company is one of the world's largest makers of commercial jet aircraft?
technology.fact: Founded in 1969 and based in São José dos Campos, Embraer is known for its E-Jet family of regional airliners.

technology.q: Brazil is a world leader in powering cars with which biofuel made from sugarcane?
technology.fact: Most new cars sold in Brazil are "flex-fuel," able to run on ethanol, gasoline or any mix of the two.

technology.q: Which Brazilian state-controlled company produces oil from the deep-water "pre-salt" fields?
technology.fact: Pre-salt oil lies beneath a thick layer of salt, kilometers below the Atlantic seabed off Brazil's southeast coast.

technology.q: Which giant hydroelectric dam on the Paraná River is shared by Brazil and Paraguay?
technology.fact: In some years Itaipu has generated more electricity than any other power plant on Earth, including China's Three Gorges.

technology.q: Which Brazilian mining company is one of the world's largest producers of iron ore?
technology.fact: Vale's Carajás complex in Pará state is among the largest iron ore mines in the world.

technology.q: Who became the first Brazilian in space, in 2006?
technology.fact: Pontes flew to the International Space Station on a Russian Soyuz in 2006, the centenary of Santos-Dumont's 14-bis flight.

technology.q: What is the name of the instant payment system launched by Brazil's Central Bank in November 2020?
technology.fact: Pix lets people send money instantly, 24 hours a day, often using just a phone number, email or QR code.

technology.q: In 1909, Carlos Chagas described a disease transmitted by which insect?
technology.fact: Chagas is celebrated for identifying the parasite, its insect vector and the disease it causes, almost single-handedly.

technology.q: What is the name of Brazil's rocket launch center, located near the equator in Maranhão?
technology.fact: Lying about 2 degrees south of the equator, Alcântara lets rockets gain extra speed from Earth's rotation, saving fuel.

art.q: Which architect designed many of Brasília's landmark modernist buildings?
art.fact: Urban planner Lúcio Costa drew Brasília's master plan, whose shape is often compared to an airplane or a bird.

art.q: Which musical style, made famous worldwide by "The Girl from Ipanema," blends samba with jazz?
art.fact: "The Girl from Ipanema" was written in 1962 by Antônio Carlos Jobim with lyrics by poet Vinicius de Moraes.

art.q: Which music and dance style drives the parades of Rio de Janeiro's Carnival?
art.fact: Rio's samba schools compete in the Sambadrome, a parade venue designed by Oscar Niemeyer and opened in 1984.

art.q: Which Afro-Brazilian martial art combines dance, music and acrobatics?
art.fact: Capoeira is played in a circle (roda) to the rhythm of the berimbau, a one-stringed musical bow.

art.q: Which Brazilian author wrote the international bestseller "The Alchemist"?
art.fact: First published in Portuguese in 1988, "The Alchemist" has been translated into more than 80 languages.

art.q: Which 19th-century novelist, author of "Dom Casmurro," was the first president of the Brazilian Academy of Letters?
art.fact: Born in 1839 to a poor family in Rio de Janeiro, Machado de Assis rose to become Brazil's most celebrated novelist.

art.q: The Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro is a famous example of which style?
art.fact: Completed in 1931, it was designed by engineer Heitor da Silva Costa with French sculptor Paul Landowski.

art.q: Which Tropicália musician later served as Brazil's Minister of Culture?
art.fact: Gil was Minister of Culture from 2003 to 2008; Tropicália mixed Brazilian rhythms with rock and psychedelia.

art.q: Which Brazilian composer wrote the "Bachianas Brasileiras"?
art.fact: Written between 1930 and 1945, the nine Bachianas Brasileiras fuse the style of J. S. Bach with Brazilian folk music.
"Abaporu" (Tupi for "man who eats people") inspired Oswald de Andrade's 1928 Anthropophagic Manifesto on "devouring" foreign culture.

politics.q: Who was Brazil's first female president, taking office in 2011?
politics.fact: An economist by training, Rousseff had served as chief of staff to her predecessor, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

politics.q: How long is a presidential term in Brazil?
politics.fact: Since a 1997 constitutional amendment, presidents may serve two consecutive terms.

politics.q: For literate Brazilian citizens aged 18 to 70, voting is:
politics.fact: Brazil has used electronic voting machines nationwide since 2000, so results are often known within hours.

politics.q: What is the name of Brazil's two-chamber federal legislature?
politics.fact: In its Niemeyer-designed home in Brasília, a dome covers the Senate chamber and an upturned bowl covers the Chamber of Deputies.

politics.q: Brazil's current constitution was promulgated in which year?
politics.fact: Ulysses Guimarães, who presided over the assembly that wrote it, dubbed it the "Citizen Constitution."

politics.q: Which president led Brazil from 1930 to 1945, including the authoritarian "Estado Novo," and again from 1951 to 1954?
politics.fact: Vargas created the state oil company Petrobras in 1953 amid the popular campaign "O petróleo é nosso" ("The oil is ours").

politics.q: Which president built Brasília, promising "fifty years of progress in five"?
politics.fact: Kubitschek, a physician by training, also drove the rapid growth of Brazil's car industry in the late 1950s.

politics.q: Not counting the Federal District, how many states does Brazil have?
politics.fact: The Federal District, home to Brasília, is a separate unit and, unlike the states, is not divided into municipalities.

politics.q: Brazil's military regime, which began in 1964, ended with a return to civilian rule in which year?
politics.fact: The 1984 "Diretas Já" movement drew millions into the streets to demand direct presidential elections.

politics.q: Which court is Brazil's highest authority on constitutional matters?
politics.fact: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) has 11 justices, nominated by the president and approved by the Senate.

current-affairs.q: Who won Brazil's October 2022 presidential election?
current-affairs.fact: Lula, who had already been president from 2003 to 2010, became the first Brazilian elected to a third presidential term.

current-affairs.q: Who served as Brazil's president from January 2019 to December 2022?
current-affairs.fact: A former army captain, Bolsonaro had served for nearly three decades as a federal deputy for Rio de Janeiro.

current-affairs.q: Which Brazilian football legend, a three-time World Cup winner, died in December 2022?
current-affairs.fact: Born Edson Arantes do Nascimento, Pelé won his first World Cup in 1958 at just 17, scoring twice in the final against Sweden.

current-affairs.q: In 2024, Brazil held the presidency of which forum of major economies, hosting its leaders' summit in Rio de Janeiro?
current-affairs.fact: At the November 2024 Rio summit, Brazil launched a Global Alliance Against Hunger and Poverty.

current-affairs.q: Which Brazilian city hosted the UN climate conference COP30 in November 2025?
current-affairs.fact: Belém, near the mouth of the Amazon, is famous for açaí and its bustling riverside Ver-o-Peso market.

current-affairs.q: Which Brazilian state suffered devastating floods in April and May 2024?
current-affairs.fact: Floodwaters closed the international airport in the state capital, Porto Alegre, for about five months.

current-affairs.q: Which Brazilian film won the Oscar for Best International Feature in March 2025?
current-affairs.fact: It was Brazil's first win in the category; its star Fernanda Torres had already won a Golden Globe for the role.

current-affairs.q: Which Brazilian gymnast won gold in the floor exercise at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
current-affairs.fact: With six Olympic medals, Andrade became Brazil's most decorated Olympian; Simone Biles and Jordan Chiles bowed to her on the podium.

current-affairs.q: In May 2024, FIFA chose Brazil to host which tournament, the first time it will be held in South America?
current-affairs.fact: Brazil previously hosted the men's World Cup in 1950 and 2014.

current-affairs.q: Which 18-year-old Brazilian won the Next Gen ATP Finals tennis tournament in December 2024?
current-affairs.fact: Brazil's best-known tennis star before him, Gustavo "Guga" Kuerten, won the French Open in 1997, 2000 and 2001.

general.q: What is the official language of Brazil?
general.fact: Brazil has more Portuguese speakers than all other Portuguese-speaking countries combined.

general.q: Which is the world's largest tropical rainforest, mostly located in Brazil?
general.fact: About 60% of the Amazon rainforest lies within Brazil's borders.

general.q: Sugarloaf Mountain overlooks the bay of which Brazilian city?
general.fact: A cable car has carried visitors toward Sugarloaf's summit since 1912, making it one of the oldest in the world.

general.q: How many men's FIFA World Cups has Brazil won?
general.fact: Brazil is the only nation to have played in every men's World Cup tournament.

general.q: What is Brazil's largest city by population?
general.fact: Brazil has the largest population of Japanese descent outside Japan, centered on São Paulo's Liberdade district.

general.q: Which black bean and pork stew is often called Brazil's national dish?
general.fact: Feijoada is traditionally served with rice, collard greens, orange slices and farofa (toasted manioc flour).

general.q: Which spectacular waterfalls lie on the border between Brazil and Argentina?
general.fact: Iguazu is made up of about 275 individual drops, the most dramatic being the U-shaped Devil's Throat.

general.q: What is the name of Brazil's currency?
general.fact: The real was introduced in 1994 under the "Plano Real," which ended years of hyperinflation.

general.q: Which is the world's largest tropical wetland, located mostly in Brazil?
general.fact: The Pantanal is one of the best places on Earth to see wild jaguars, along with capybaras, caimans and giant otters.

general.q: The colorful historic Pelourinho district, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is in which Brazilian city?
general.fact: Founded in 1549, Salvador was Brazil's first colonial capital and is a vibrant center of Afro-Brazilian culture.
